messages.subject: Autologistic Occupancy Parameterization
parts:
Hi all,

I was curious of peoples experiences with dynamic (multiseason) occupancy models in WinBUGS/JAGS/NIMBLE or even in Stan. In particular, how important is the auto logistic parameterization (see Royle and Dorado 2008 book cap 9) vs the direct colonization/survival parameterization of Royle and Kery 2007 and used in Kery and Schaub (2012)? The model will have covariates and random effects although I’m fairly indifferent to modeling them on psi vs. gamma and phi in terms of inference for this project. The auto logistic parameterization has advantages in terms of MCMC performance but is more difficult to interpret and messier to code. I just don’t know how important the MCMC performance really is or if it’s just a matter of a bit longer chains with the simpler, direct parameterization. Does the posterior get estimated just as well without having to run for 10x or 100x or 1000x times as long?

Thanks for any insights,
Dan

messages.subject: RE: Autologistic Occupancy Parameterization
parts:
Dear Dan,

all depends of course, but in general I have observed decent mixing with the fully dynamic occupancy models in WinBUGS and JAGS, even for reasonably big data sets (e.g., couple of thousand sites and up to 20-30 or so years).  So I would just try out and see how it goes.

Best regards  ---- Marc
